state.target_treatment: Assignment of ground-based silver-iodide cloud seeding to Sierra Madre or Medicine Bow during a four-hour experimental unit (EU).
state.scope: The 118 quality-controlled EUs used in the WWMPP primary analysis. One EU includes the paired ranges. Target sites are HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow); auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment.

evidence.location: Section 2, Figure 1 explanation, and Table 1 with its caption, pp. 2640-2643
evidence.text: Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot. The authors report 154 EUs, 27 precipitation-QC exclusions, and nine additional generator-performance exclusions, leaving 118 for the primary analysis. The monthly generator-exclusion cells in Table 1 sum to eight, while its margins and the prose report nine; the retained count here follows the authors' reported totals.
The design has eight generators per range and multiple precipitation gauges; gauge QC is conducted without knowledge of seeding assignments.

The presentation shows the paired design, four-hour measurements, and a 118-case Medicine Bow assignment plot. Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding in winters 2009/10, 2011/12, and 2013/14. These are different diagnostics within the same trial reported in 2018.

q1.instructions: How are the two range-level seeding assignments related within one retained EU? Select exactly one option. Use other only when the evidence establishes an answer outside the substantive alternatives. Use not_stated when missing, incomplete, or ambiguous supplied evidence prevents this judgment without unresolved incompatible statements. Use conflicting only for unresolved incompatible evidence about this same judgment and scope.

criteria.independent_assignments: Each range is independently randomized, so both or neither can be assigned seeding within that EU.
criteria.complementary_assignment: One joint allocation selects the seeded range, and the other range receives the complementary unseeded assignment.
criteria.both_seeded: Both ranges are assigned seeding together as one treated pair.
criteria.permanent_range: One range is permanently assigned seeding and the other remains unseeded throughout the study.
criteria.other: The evidence establishes a different substantive answer from those listed.
criteria.not_stated: The supplied evidence does not establish the requested judgment.
criteria.conflicting: The supplied evidence contains unresolved incompatible accounts of this judgment and scope.

q2.instructions: Does an assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure to seeding material in this study? Select exactly one option. Use not_stated when missing, incomplete, or ambiguous supplied evidence prevents this judgment without unresolved incompatible statements. Use conflicting only for unresolved incompatible evidence about this same judgment and scope.

criteria.zero_exposure_established: Yes; assignment to the unseeded range establishes that it received no seeding material.
criteria.assignment_only: No; it establishes the planned allocation, while physical exposure requires additional evidence because cross-range contamination is discussed.
criteria.exposure_confirmed_everywhere: No; the label establishes that every unseeded range-period was physically exposed to seeding material.
criteria.not_stated: The supplied evidence does not establish the requested judgment.
criteria.conflicting: The supplied evidence contains unresolved incompatible accounts of this judgment and scope.
